- When sentiment is negative or shows early signs of decline (e.g., -0.25 or 0.00 after positive), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75% from prior 18-day mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above recent peak for next 7 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or positive (e.g., 0.50 or above), model frequently overestimates; apply downward bias of 2–5% for 3–7 day horizon.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early 30-day forecasts when sentiment is flat or mildly negative — adjust downward by 1–4% for first 5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizon; if forecast is >10% above 18-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment turns positive after negative, model often fails to adjust quickly — delay correction until sentiment stabilizes or next 3-day window.
